correctness.rationale: Cell averaging followed by Bernstein reconstruction factors K_n; the opposite composition is M, which is doubly stochastic and commutes with reflection. The BV derivative-measure decomposition (negative derivative measure if using left indicators) and Minkowski reduce the norm to jump profiles. Between consecutive grid boundaries the centered output is affine in jump position, so its L1 norm is convex and the sharp finite maximum is attained at a grid boundary. For a decreasing nonconstant coefficient vector, the derivative of its Bernstein polynomial is a sum of adjacent differences against a positive basis in (0,1), hence is strictly negative; cell averaging preserves strict order. Mean invariance gives precisely one crossing and twice the positive-part integral in (2). Binomial moments of cell averages of monomials give the distinct diagonal eigenvalues (n)_k/(n+1)^k; in particular the centered affine mode is h. For i and j left of center, M_ij-M_i,n-j is strictly positive because b_j>b_n-j throughout the interior of each such cell. Perron–Frobenius and antisymmetric extension give the strict sign pattern of w, normalized using w dot h=1. The spectral projection h w^T and integral of |x-1/2|=1/4 yield A_n and the uniform lower-mode error for fixed n. The strict gap in the magnitudes of partial sums excludes noncentral grid boundaries eventually, and reflection keeps the central pair tied when n is even. In degree one the sole nonconstant mode gives 2^(-r-1) exactly. Inspected the frozen checker without executing it. In an independent exact-arithmetic computation using a binomial-tail primitive for M and polynomial spectral projectors, all five displayed A_n and their grid index sets passed.
residual_risks: Fixed-degree asymptotics only. The statement identifies maximizing grid indices eventually; the proof does not assume all-iterate centrality.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The diagonal expansion yields the fixed-n exponent and a leading linear functional, but not its optimum on the BV unit ball or strict signs and gap of its cumulative grid weights. originality.rationale: Cooper–Waldron already identifies the exact spectrum, the derivative intertwining with the point-sampling operator, and the diagonal expansion including dual modes. Do not credit those ingredients as new. The checked primary passages and indexed near-matches do not yield the all-iterate sharp BV-to-L1 mean-mixing norm or the strict-sign argument identifying the locations that optimize its leading amplitude. Related same-day records are distinguished by the actual operator, residual and norm, not by a presumed order.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalent operator norm results or additional analysis of the known dual functional may exist. Catalogue date alone does not establish priority.

value.rationale: The sharp distance from equilibrium on the BV unit ball is a natural mixing quantity sensitive to discontinuities. The theorem replaces an optimization over all BV inputs with a finite root-and-integral computation for every power and identifies the worst grid locations and sharp rational amplitude at long times. These quantitative facts are not determined just by the known spectral gap.
residual_risks: No uniform-in-degree asymptotic, effective general cutoff or centrality at every finite iterate is asserted.
